item.title: The Evolution of Stablecoins: A New Era for Global Finance
item.dc:creator: dForce
item.content:encoded:
The cryptocurrency ecosystem has witnessed extraordinary transformations since Bitcoin’s inception in 2009. Yet, perhaps no innovation has proven as essential to bridging traditional finance with decentralized technology as stablecoins. In just over a decade, stablecoins have evolved from obscure experimental tokens to cornerstones of the global digital economy, commanding a market exceeding $330 billion (source). Today, as CNH (offshore yuan) stablecoins emerge on the global stage, we stand at the threshold of a multi-currency digital future — one that promises to reshape cross-border trade, financial inclusion, and monetary policy itself.

This comprehensive guide traces the history of stablecoins in crypto, exploring their origins, failures, triumphs, and the exciting potential of CNH-backed stablecoins that are poised to revolutionize global finance.

🔮 The Genesis: Early Stablecoin Experiments (2014–2017)

BitUSD: The Pioneer (2014)

The world’s first stablecoin, BitUSD, launched on July 21, 2014, on the BitShares blockchain. Created by cryptocurrency visionaries Dan Larimer (later of EOS fame) and Charles Hoskinson (Cardano founder), BitUSD represented a bold attempt to solve crypto’s most persistent problem: volatility.

BitUSD was a crypto-collateralized stablecoin, backed by the BitShares core token (BTS). The concept was revolutionary — users could mint BitUSD by locking up BTS as collateral, creating a digital asset pegged 1:1 to the US dollar. Unfortunately, BitUSD’s reliance on a volatile, relatively obscure collateral asset proved fatal. When BitShares’ price collapsed, BitUSD lost its peg in 2018 and never recovered.

NuBits: Another Early Casualty (2014)

Also launched in 2014, NuBits took a different approach by using Bitcoin as collateral. While Bitcoin offered greater liquidity than BitShares, it remained highly volatile. When Bitcoin’s price plummeted, NuBits’ reserves proved insufficient and undiversified. The stablecoin collapsed, eventually trading around $0.04.

Tether (USDT): The Game-Changer (2014)

In October 2014, a project initially called Realcoin — later rebranded as Tether (USDT) — quietly launched on the Bitcoin blockchain via the Omni Layer protocol. Unlike its predecessors, Tether adopted a radically simpler model: fiat-backed reserves. For every USDT minted, Tether Limited claimed to hold one US dollar in reserve. This 1:1 fiat-backing model proved transformative. Tether addressed the core weakness of earlier stablecoins: it eliminated reliance on volatile crypto collateral. By 2025, Tether has grown to a market capitalization exceeding $183 billion, making it the largest and most traded cryptocurrency by volume, accounting for more than 50% of the stablecoin market.

📈 The Maturation Phase: Diversification and Innovation (2017–2022)

USD Coin (USDC): Transparency and Compliance (2018)

As Tether faced ongoing scrutiny over reserve transparency, USD Coin (USDC) emerged in September 2018 as a response. Launched by Circle and Coinbase, USDC prioritized regulatory compliance and audited reserves, partnering with financial giants like BlackRock and BNY Mellon.

USDC quickly gained institutional trust, reaching a market cap of $76.53 billion. Its success underscored a crucial shift: transparency and regulatory alignment were becoming non-negotiable for mainstream adoption.

DAI: Decentralized Stability (2017)

In 2017, MakerDAO introduced DAI, a decentralized, crypto-backed stablecoin that represented a hybrid approach. To mint DAI, users must deposit $1.70 worth of Ethereum for every $1.00 DAI — creating a 70% buffer against volatility.

Critically, DAI diversified its reserves beyond Ethereum, incorporating fiat-backed stablecoins like USDC (comprising ~42% of reserves) and Wrapped Bitcoin. This diversification strategy has allowed DAI to maintain its peg through multiple market crashes, currently holding a $5.37 billion market cap.

dForce’s USX: The Omni-Yield Stablecoin (2021)

Over-collateralized by crypto assets, USX from dForce introduces a paradigm shift: omni-yield generation across blockchains. USX is dForce’s native decentralized stablecoin, designed for cross-chain interoperability, composability, and — most importantly — earning yield for holders.

The standout feature is sUSX, the staked version of USX. USX stakers on https://app.usx.finance/#/sUSX receive omni savings yield regardless of which blockchain they’re on. This transforms USX from a static settlement layer into a yield-generating asset, competing directly with money market funds and savings accounts.

Current Yield: sUSX currently offers 5% APY, with yield sourced from:

  • Protocol revenue from lending and vault operations
  • Real-world asset yields from tokenized investments
  • Cross-chain liquidity fees
  • Protocol governance mechanisms

The TerraUSD Collapse: A Cautionary Tale (2022)

In May 2022, the algorithmic stablecoin TerraUSD (UST) spectacularly collapsed, losing nearly all its value within days. UST relied on arbitrage incentives and algorithmic supply adjustments — not tangible reserves — to maintain its peg.

When market panic triggered mass redemptions, UST’s mechanisms failed catastrophically. Despite the Luna Foundation Guard holding over 70,000 bitcoins in reserves, it couldn’t stem the collapse. Today, UST trades at approximately $0.02.

⚖️ The Current Landscape: Regulatory Clarity and Global Expansion (2023–2025)

Regulatory Milestones

The stablecoin ecosystem has matured rapidly alongside evolving regulations:

  • July 18, 2025: The US GENIUS Act established the first comprehensive federal framework for dollar-pegged stablecoins, mandating 100% reserves in liquid assets (predominantly US Treasuries).
  • June 30, 2024: The EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation took effect, categorizing stablecoins into electronic money tokens (EMTs) and asset-referenced tokens (ARTs).

These frameworks provide the regulatory clarity that institutional capital demands, catalyzing legitimacy and adoption.

The Rise of CNH Stablecoins: A Paradigm Shift

For over a decade, the stablecoin market has been dominated by USD-pegged assets, entrenching dollar hegemony in digital finance. Nearly 99% of stablecoins are pegged to the US dollar, reinforcing American financial infrastructure globally.

CNH (offshore yuan) stablecoins represent a transformative development:

  1. Cross-Border Trade Efficiency: CNH stablecoins enable 24/7 instant settlement for this massive economic corridor, bypassing slow, expensive correspondent banking.
  2. Yuan Internationalization: The yuan’s share of global payments is at 2.88% in June 2025. CNH stablecoins provide digital rails for RMB adoption without requiring full capital account liberalization.
  3. Alternative to Dollar Dominance: By offering a blockchain-based alternative to USDT and USDC, CNH stablecoins reduce systemic reliance on the dollar and create a multi-currency digital ecosystem.
  4. Financial Inclusion and Innovation: Stablecoins make yuan-denominated finance accessible to underserved markets where dollar liquidity is scarce.

✨ Conclusion

The history of stablecoins is a story of relentless innovation, hard-learned lessons, and transformative potential. From the failed experiments of BitUSD and NuBits to the dominance of Tether and USDC, stablecoins have evolved into indispensable infrastructure for the digital economy..

As the world moves toward a multi-currency, blockchain-enabled financial system, CNH stablecoins stand at the forefront of this revolution. For investors, businesses, and policymakers, the message is clear: CNH stablecoins are not just promising — they are essential to the future of money.

item.title: DeFi Yield 2.0 and Beyond: AI’s Full Spectrum of Optimization
item.dc:creator: dForce
item.content:encoded:
DeFi has rapidly evolved from a niche experiment into a multi-billion-dollar ecosystem. Early adopters chased high yields by manually migrating funds between lending protocols, liquidity pools, and farms — often at the expense of time, convenience, and capital efficiency. As the landscape grows more complex, manual yield strategies no longer suffice. Today’s DeFi spans dozens of chains, hundreds of protocols, and thousands of pools, each with its own risks, rewards, and fee structures.

Enter AI-driven DeFi optimization, a new paradigm where intelligent agents take over the heavy lifting — continuously monitoring markets, executing transactions, and protecting capital. What began as basic auto-compounding scripts has blossomed into a fully autonomous system that adapts strategies in real time, balances risk, and orchestrates cross-chain movements, all without human intervention.

The Manual Yield Farming Dilemma

Yield farmers initially relied on dashboards and spreadsheets to track APYs, gas costs, and protocol health. Every reinvestment required:

  • Gas-heavy transactions across multiple chains
  • Constant vigilance for yield spikes or protocol vulnerabilities
  • Manual bridging with slippage and delay risks

Over time, these tasks became unsustainable for most users. Meanwhile, smart error-prone bots emerged, but they still followed rigid rules, missing sudden market moves or executing during peak fees.

Nine AI Optimizations Powering DeFi 2.0

AI agents now inject continuous intelligence into every facet of yield farming — from cost-aware execution to real-time risk management. By leveraging machine learning and on-chain data, these agents transform rigid, schedule-based compounding into a dynamic, always-on optimization engine. The following nine innovations illustrate how AI is reshaping DeFi, delivering higher, more stable returns and a seamless user experience.

Dynamic Rebalancing Across Protocols

Continuously shifts allocations to the highest-yielding, safest pools based on live APY, liquidity, and risk scores.

Liquidity Buffer Management

Maintains a reserve calibrated to withdrawal patterns, ensuring instant redemptions without draining yield.

Cost-Aware Execution

Times transactions for low-fee windows or batches operations to minimize gas impact on net returns.

Cross-Chain Orchestration

Automates trust-minimized asset transfers, synchronizing portfolios across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, BNB Chain, and more.

Risk-Adjusted Strategy Selection

Integrates on-chain health checks and off-chain sentiment signals, pivoting away from risky pools in real time.

Customizable Risk-Return Profiles

Builds bespoke portfolios based on user preferences — max drawdown, target volatility, or thematic filters.

Continuous Performance Auditing

Real-time dashboards and anomaly detectors flag underperformance or suspicious activity immediately.

Auto-Governance & Parameter Tuning

Proposes DAO parameter updates — like fee adjustments — based on analytics, shortening decision cycles.

Composable Third-Party Integrations

Exposes SDKs and widgets for wallets, dashboards, and chatbots to embed AI strategies with a single snippet.

The Three Phases of Yield Farming and Compounding

One of the clearest differences and opportunities made possible by AI can be seen in how funds are moved, and restaked to achieve compound interest: here’s how it all evolved since the earliest days of DeFi.

Phase 1: Manual Reinvestments

We started building in 2019, so we know that in the earliest days of DeFi, yield farming was a hands-on affair. Investors tracked earnings with pen and paper or through an excel sheet, reinvested rewards manually, and juggled risk by intuition. Timing was critical, and missing the best window meant lost opportunity or exposure.

Phase 2: Basic Auto-Compounding

Platforms began offering scripts and contracts that would periodically collect and reinvest rewards. This made compounding easier, scheduling transactions to follow regular cycles. However, these tools remained “dumb” — reacting only to fixed instructions, ignorant of market volatility, cost spikes, or new opportunities.

Phase 3: AI-Driven Compounding

The present and future introduce AI agents that never sleep. These smart systems monitor yields, liquidity, fees, and risk factors in real time — reinvesting and reallocating capital dynamically across protocols and chains. They anticipate change, learn from the market, and maximize earnings proactively, freeing users from both micromanagement and manual strategy.

Looking Ahead

The shift from manual and rule-based bots to intelligent, autonomous agents marks a turning point for DeFi. Investors no longer need to chase yields or monitor gas — AI does it all, adapting strategies to ever-changing markets. dForce is ahead of this movement, with a cutting hedge protocol that is being developed as we speak. In the era of Auto-Compounding 2.0 and beyond, your capital works smarter, not harder — reinventing what it means to farm yield in a decentralized world. Stay tuned to learn how to leverage AI to optimize your yield with dForce!

item.title: How AI Yield Aggregators Work: Inside the Tech Powering DeFAI
item.dc:creator: dForce
item.content:encoded:
The world of Decentralized Finance has always promised open, permissionless access to yield opportunities. Yet for many users, yield farming and liquidity provision remain complex, requiring constant monitoring and manual strategy adjustments. Enter the new frontier: AI yield aggregators.

By combining the intelligence of autonomous AI agents with the transparency of blockchain, these next-generation tools represent a shift toward what we call DeFAI — the convergence of DeFi and Artificial Intelligence. At dForce, we are building this future by introducing an AI agent layer to optimize yield in real time, especially for RWA-backed vaults and stablecoins.

This article takes a closer look at how AI yield aggregators work, from data ingestion to smart contract execution, and why they mark the next evolution in onchain finance.

The Challenge: Manual Yield Aggregation

Traditional DeFi yield aggregators rely on pre-programmed strategies. While effective to some degree, they have limitations:

  • Static logic: Strategies are coded once and rarely adapt dynamically to fast-changing markets.
  • High monitoring costs: Users still need to track yields, fees, and risks manually.
  • Limited scope: Many platforms only focus on crypto-native pools, leaving out tokenized real-world assets (RWAs).

The result? A landscape where sophisticated yield strategies remain accessible mainly to experts.

The AI-Powered Upgrade: Smarter Aggregation with Agents

AI yield aggregators introduce a new paradigm: autonomous optimization. Instead of static strategies, AI agents dynamically learn, adapt, and execute on behalf of users.

At dForce, our AI agent layer is being designed to interact directly with DeFi protocols and RWA vaults, enabling real-time, intelligent decision-making.

Let’s break down the core architecture:

1. Data Ingestion & Analysis

AI yield aggregators thrive on data. Agents continuously consume:

  • Onchain signals: Liquidity levels, collateralization ratios, lending rates, governance changes.
  • Offchain data: Macroeconomic indicators, RWA performance metrics, market sentiment.
  • Cross-protocol feeds: Comparing yields across multiple blockchains and pools.

With this information, AI agents don’t just react — they predict opportunities and risks.

2. Strategy Formulation in Real Time

Instead of relying on a fixed farming script, AI agents create dynamic strategies:

  • Identify the highest risk-adjusted yield opportunities.
  • Model portfolio allocations to balance yield, liquidity, and risk.
  • Update strategies continuously as new data flows in.

This adaptive logic mirrors what professional asset managers do — but with machine-speed precision.

3. Smart Contract Execution

Once a decision is made, AI agents directly interact with dForce’s smart contracts:

  • Rebalancing vaults to capture better yields.
  • Adjusting lending parameters based on liquidity conditions.
  • Swapping assets to diversify exposure or mitigate risks.

Because execution happens onchain, every action is transparent, verifiable, and aligned with user permissions.

4. Feedback Loop & Optimization

AI agents continuously refine their strategies through reinforcement learning:

  • Successful outcomes (e.g., higher net yield) strengthen models.
  • Poor outcomes are adjusted out of future strategies.

This feedback loop ensures the system improves over time — something no static yield aggregator can achieve.

Why This Matters: Unlocking the Promise of DeFAI

The benefits of AI-driven yield aggregation go far beyond efficiency:

  • Accessibility: Complex DeFi strategies become available to everyday users without deep technical knowledge.
  • Risk Management: AI agents monitor for anomalies, issue alerts, and take proactive action to protect assets.
  • RWA Integration: AI agents will make it seamless to manage tokenized real-world assets..
  • Always-On Optimization: No more sleepless nights monitoring yield changes — AI agents work 24/7.

dForce and the Future of AI Yield Aggregation

dForce is pioneering the DeFAI era, where DeFi meets AI to unlock smarter, safer, and more profitable financial tools. By embedding AI agent layers into our RWA vaults and DeFi markets, we aim to become the onchain gateway for intelligent yield management.

This is more than an upgrade. It’s the future of finance: self-optimizing, data-driven, and accessible to all.

Final Thoughts

AI yield aggregators are transforming how value flows in DeFi. They replace static, manual strategies with adaptive, autonomous optimization, setting a new standard for yield farming, risk management, and liquidity provision.

At dForce, we’re building the infrastructure to make this future a reality. Stay tuned as we unveil more about our AI agent-powered vaults and how you can be among the first to benefit.

👉 Follow dForce on Twitter for updates, and join our community on Telegram to participate in the DeFAI revolution.

item.title: The Rise of AI Agents in DeFi: From Manual Yield Farming to Autonomous Optimization
item.dc:creator: dForce
item.content:encoded:
DeFi has always been about one thing: unlocking smarter ways to make capital work onchain. From the early days of manual yield farming to today’s sophisticated vaults and aggregators, the space has evolved at breakneck speed. Now, a new frontier is emerging — AI agents that autonomously manage and optimize yield strategies.

At dForce, we see this as a defining shift for DeFi. While the first wave of DeFi rewarded users who were willing to monitor dashboards around the clock, the next wave belongs to intelligent agents that can do the work for you, and we are closely look this trend.

📈 From Manual Yield Farming to Smarter Aggregation

In 2020, DeFi yield farming captured global attention. Users manually rotated assets across liquidity pools, lending markets, and farms, chasing the highest APYs. While profitable for some, this model had clear downsides:

  • Time-intensive → constant monitoring and transactions
  • High friction → gas costs and complex user flows, especially with strategies involving multiple chains
  • Risky → manual errors and impermanent loss

DeFi yield aggregators simplified this by pooling user funds and automating strategies. Yet even these solutions are fundamentally static: they follow pre-programmed strategies that don’t adapt fast enough to volatile markets.

🤖 Enter AI Agents: Autonomous Yield Optimizers

AI agents change the game. Instead of fixed strategies, these are dynamic, self-learning systems capable of:

  • Real-time yield scouting → scanning dozens of protocols simultaneously
  • Portfolio rebalancing → moving liquidity where it earns most, automatically
  • Risk-adjusted optimization → considering volatility, liquidity, and counterparty risks
  • Natural language interfaces → users can set goals in plain language (e.g., “safe stable yield” or “balanced growth”)

In short, AI agents are to yield farming what algorithmic trading was to traditional finance — a leap from manual execution to intelligent automation.

🚀 The Road Ahead: DeFAI at dForce

At dForce, we believe the fusion of AI + DeFi = DeFAI is the natural evolution of onchain finance. By integrating AI agents with our RWA vaults, we aim to make yield optimization:

  • Smarter → adaptive, real-time strategies
  • Safer → AI-powered risk monitoring and response
  • More Accessible → seamless experiences for global users, especially in China

This is just the beginning — more details on dForce’s DeFAI initiative will be shared soon.

📢 Join the Conversation

The age of DeFAI is coming — and dForce is building it. Stay tuned for our upcoming announcements, and follow us on Twitter and Telegram to be the first to learn how AI agents will transform onchain yield optimization.

🌏 The Greater China Opportunity

Greater China — encompassing Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan — is home to one of the most dynamic and diverse economies in the world. With a GDP exceeding $20 trillion, the region boasts a vast range of assets: real estate, infrastructure, manufacturing, supply chain finance, private credit, and emerging tech ventures.

Beyond sheer scale, Greater China’s assets are deeply embedded in global trade and investment flows. Initiatives like the Belt and Road Initiative have expanded economic corridors across Asia, Europe, and Africa, creating new avenues for cross-border financing and infrastructure development.

Yet, tapping into this wealth remains challenging. Regulatory frameworks are evolving, capital markets are complex, and access for global investors is often limited.

🔓 The ABC of why Greater China’s RWAs Need an On-Chain Gateway

🚀 A. Unlocking Illiquidity & Expanding Access

Traditional asset markets come with high barriers and geographic limits:

  • Long settlement times
  • Restricted investor participation
  • High minimum investment thresholds

Tokenization changes this game:

  • Fractional Ownership → Investors can hold and trade smaller portions of high-value assets.
  • Global Reach → Access to a worldwide pool of capital, 24/7.
  • Faster Transactions → On-chain settlement in minutes.

🛠 B. Enhancing Efficiency & Transparency

Blockchain brings operational clarity to processes that were once opaque:

  • Streamlined Transfers and due diligence workflows
  • Lower Costs by reducing intermediaries
  • Immutable Records for compliance, audits, and trust

💴 C. The Strategic Importance of RMB-Denominated Assets

As the Chinese Yuan (RMB) rises in global influence, we expect offshore RMB (CNH) to become a vital tool in international trade and finance. Efficient digital pathways for RMB-based assets have the potential to drive new cross-border liquidity flows and cement the RMB’s global role.

Here are its features:

🔮 The Future of Finance, Powered by dForce and China’s RWAs

By tokenizing a significant portion of the world’s real-world assets, we are building a more inclusive, transparent, and efficient global financial system — one where Greater China’s economic strength is accessible to all.

item.title: Navigating the Dragon’s Path: Regulatory Frameworks for China’s On-Chain RWAs
item.dc:creator: dForce
item.content:encoded:
In the rapidly evolving world of digital finance, real-world assets (RWAs) tokenized on blockchain are emerging as a bridge between traditional finance and decentralized innovation. But their institutional adoption hinges on one critical factor: regulatory clarity.

China, long known for its stringent approach to cryptocurrency, paradoxically stands among the world’s most enthusiastic adopters of blockchain infrastructure. This duality has positioned Hong Kong as a vital regulatory sandbox — a gateway for testing and deploying on-chain innovations under supervised conditions.

As global financial centers rush to define the rules of tokenized finance, China’s moves — particularly around RMB-backed stablecoins — deserve close scrutiny. Could a yuan-denominated stablecoin issued offshore transform the global RWA landscape? And can Hong Kong’s new stablecoin ordinance pave the way for compliant, scalable on-chain finance?

🇨🇳 China’s Stance: Blockchain Embrace, Crypto Caution

For over a decade, Beijing has maintained a cautious — if not adversarial — stance toward cryptocurrencies. Crackdowns on trading and mining in 2021 served as a clear message. But behind the scenes, a different story has been unfolding: one of state-driven blockchain adoption.

  • The Digital Yuan (e-CNY) is already in pilot use across major Chinese cities.
  • Leading Chinese companies — Ant Group, JD.com — are lobbying to launch offshore yuan stablecoins.
  • Beijing sees stablecoins not as threats, but as tools to improve cross-border payments and enhance the internationalization of the renminbi (RMB).

This shift reflects a broader strategic vision: decouple crypto from speculation, and use regulated, blockchain-based assets to reinforce state monetary policy.

China’s Stance: Blockchain Embrace, Crypto Caution

For over a decade, Beijing has maintained a cautious — if not adversarial — stance toward cryptocurrencies. Crackdowns on trading and mining in 2021 served as a clear message. But behind the scenes, a different story has been unfolding: one of state-driven blockchain adoption.

  • The Digital Yuan (e-CNY) is already in pilot use across major Chinese cities.
  • Leading Chinese companies — Ant Group, JD.com — are lobbying to launch offshore yuan stablecoins.
  • Beijing sees stablecoins not as threats, but as tools to improve cross-border payments and enhance the internationalization of the renminbi (RMB).

This shift reflects a broader strategic vision: decouple crypto from speculation, and use regulated, blockchain-based assets to reinforce state monetary policy.

🏦 Hong Kong’s Role as a Regulatory Bridge

Enter Hong Kong — a Special Administrative Region with legal autonomy, global financial credibility, and deep integration with mainland China.

In 2024, the Hong Kong Legislative Council passed the Stablecoin Ordinance, establishing a licensing regime for fiat-backed stablecoin issuers. The law, effective August 1st, includes:

  • Strict capital reserve requirements (100% backing in cash or equivalents).
  • Monthly independent audits and public reserve disclosures.
  • T+0 redemption guarantees for stablecoin holders.
  • Physical presence and local incorporation mandates for issuers.

With over 40 firms preparing license applications, including tech giants and state-affiliated financial institutions, Hong Kong is positioning itself as a global hub for compliant RWAs and regulated stablecoins.

🔎 Why Regulatory Clarity Matters for On-Chain RWAs

The tokenization of assets like bonds, invoices, and real estate depends on three pillars:

  1. Legal certainty around asset ownership and rights.
  2. Interoperability with financial infrastructure (banking, custody, KYC/AML).
  3. Trust in the value peg, especially for stablecoins used in RWA settlement.

China’s approach — leveraging Hong Kong to pilot offshore RMB stablecoins (CNH-backed) — is a blueprint for de-risking RWA adoption. Instead of speculative tokens, these stablecoins are framed as regulated digital representations of fiat — subject to stringent oversight, reserve transparency, and cross-border compliance.

This model appeals to institutional players — banks, insurers, asset managers — who require regulatory alignment before moving real assets on-chain.

💡 Offshore RMB Stablecoins: Strategic Implications

The idea of a yuan stablecoin is more than a technical experiment — it’s a geopolitical and economic play.

  • A CNH stablecoin could accelerate RMB internationalization in trade, lending, and settlements.
  • It offers a non-dollar-denominated stable asset for emerging markets seeking alternatives.
  • It enables cross-border payments outside of legacy systems like SWIFT.

But the stakes are high. Such a move challenges dollar hegemony — not just in trade, but now in on-chain liquidity. Today, USD stablecoins (USDT, USDC) dominate DeFi. Could a compliant RMB stablecoin offer a credible alternative?

🚧 Challenges Ahead

Despite the progress, key challenges remain:

  • Capital controls: RMB convertibility is still partially restricted.
  • Market trust: Will global users adopt RMB tokens over USD ones?
  • Geopolitics: U.S. pressure could limit RMB stablecoin integration in allied jurisdictions.
  • Ecosystem support: Wallets, exchanges, and on/off ramps must adapt to support new stablecoins.

Success will require regulatory diplomacy, financial infrastructure upgrades, and ongoing transparency to compete with USD-pegged stablecoins’ global dominance.

🧭 Conclusion: China’s RWA Game Plan Is Taking Shape

The global contest for on-chain monetary dominance is underway — and China, through Hong Kong, is placing a major bet. By focusing on compliant, transparent, and purpose-built stablecoins, Beijing may not seek to dethrone the dollar overnight, but rather to carve out a parallel, interoperable system — one where the renminbi flows freely in digital form, facilitating trade, lending, and settlement across emerging markets and digital finance rails.

For builders and institutions exploring tokenized RWAs, this signals one thing: China is opening the gate — carefully, but deliberately. Understanding its regulatory frameworks today could mean unlocking strategic opportunities tomorrow, and we at dForce are ahead of this movement!

item.dc:creator: MGGYY
item.content:encoded:
The Rise of RMB Stablecoins — and Why It Matters for DeFAI

In a crypto world long dominated by USD-based stablecoins, a quiet shift is taking place. RMB-pegged stablecoins are beginning to emerge, offering a compelling alternative that could reshape the global financial landscape — and DeFAI protocols like dForce are taking notice.

As we move into the second half of 2025, it’s becoming increasingly clear: the next chapter of stablecoin evolution might be written in Renminbi.

Why RMB Stablecoins Matter

While over 99% of stablecoin volume still revolves around USD-backed assets like USDT, USDC, and DAI, this concentration presents a structural risk — exposing the global DeFi ecosystem to U.S. financial policies and regulatory uncertainty.

RMB stablecoins offer a viable counterweight. Here’s why they’re gaining traction:

1. ✅ RMB-Denominated Trade and Settlement

RMB stablecoins can radically simplify cross-border transactions:

  • Faster, cheaper settlement across jurisdictions without intermediaries
  • Reduced reliance on banks for RMB remittances and payments
  • Lower currency conversion friction, especially for countries trading with China

As digital trade expands, RMB stablecoins could become the backbone of Asia-led settlement rails.

2. 🌐 Boosting RMB Internationalization

RMB stablecoins are more than a tool — they’re part of a broader strategic push by China to internationalize its currency. These digital assets:

  • Offer a hedge against dollar dominance
  • Increase global liquidity and accessibility of the RMB
  • Provide a neutral medium for international trade in an increasingly multipolar world

3. 💵 A DeFi-Friendly Alternative to USD Stablecoins

DeFi markets have long lacked a non-USD stable asset that’s liquid and integrated across protocols. RMB stablecoins fill that gap:

  • Enable borrowing/lending in RMB
  • Introduce new yield opportunities uncorrelated with the U.S. rate cycle
  • Reduce systemic risk in multi-currency strategies

For protocols like dForce, this opens up a new design space — a place where DeFi liquidity meets East Asian monetary flows.

4. 🏗 Gateway for Onchain RWAs in China

China is home to massive real-world asset ecosystems — from receivables and infrastructure to tokenized gold and real estate. RMB stablecoins enable:

  • Tokenization and settlement of Chinese RWAs
  • Onchain financing for Chinese issuers via composable, compliant DeFi primitives

RWA vaults on dForce could tap into this ecosystem, bridging permissioned finance and open protocols in unprecedented ways.

5. 🚀 Hong Kong as the Web3 Launchpad

With Hong Kong advancing as Asia’s regulatory sandbox for Web3 and digital finance, RMB stablecoins are positioned to thrive:

  • Hong Kong-based issuers are launching regulated RMB stablecoins
  • These tokens can become regional liquidity hubs across Layer 1s and Layer 2s

As the U.S. experiments with its “Strategic Bitcoin Reserve,” China may counter with digital RMB liquidity rails — and dForce is watching this evolution closely.

6. 🧩 Complementing China’s CBDC

China’s e-CNY is tightly controlled and not built for open, permissionless protocols. RMB stablecoins, on the other hand:

  • Coexist with CBDCs
  • Power public DeFi, NFTs, RWA vaults, and global integrations

That’s where protocols like dForce come in — programmable, composable, and open for innovation.

🔧 What’s Next for dForce?

dForce is actively exploring ways to integrate RMB stablecoins into its protocol stack through:

  • RMB-denominated lending markets on Unitus.finance
  • RWA vaults tied to infrastructure and SME assets in Greater China
  • AI Agents that manage yield strategies across RMB stablecoins

The goal? Build a programmable DeFAI layer that meets real-world capital where it’s headed — not where it’s been.

🧠 Final Thoughts

RMB stablecoins are no longer just a theoretical construct — they’re fast becoming a geopolitical and financial reality. As global DeFi matures, the space must evolve beyond its USD roots.

At dForce, we are closely monitoring the landscape, as we believe the convergence of RMB stablecoins, RWA markets, and autonomous DeFAI infrastructure represents a major leap forward.

Stay tuned!
